parsed.population_and_sample: Rural communities in northern Ghana, including Mognore, Sapeliga, and Kugrasia; 29 interviewees consisting of local leaders, politicians, and farmers (13 women, 16 men).
parsed.exposure: Participation in the Local Trans-boundary Water Committee (PAGEV project) and implementation of river bank restoration policies.
parsed.outcome: Changes in water access for irrigation, livelihood vulnerability, and elite capture of governance participation mechanisms.
parsed.rationale: The study empirically examines how a local trans-boundary water committee (an institutional/governance factor) impacts rural household water access for irrigation. Through qualitative interviews (Section 4), the author analyzes the outcomes of these governance interventions, specifically noting how the creation of farming-free buffer zones restricted irrigation access for poor farmers (Section 4.2, 5.1).
